heading: INT. LAMPLIGHTERS' GUILD HALL - LONDON - 1872 - EVENING

units.text: INT. LAMPLIGHTERS' GUILD HALL - LONDON - 1872 - EVENING
A long timber room hung with tin ladders and coiled wicks.
Rain on the high windows.
Five brass lamps burn along a table.
ELIAS THORNBY, fifties, guild master, sits at the head in a velvet waistcoat gone bald at the elbows.
AGATHA PRUDHOE, forties, a widow with a ledger, sits at his right.
CONSTABLE JOLLIFFE, thirties, damp and unhappy, stands at the door.
MRS. QUILL, sixties, the hall's cook, brings a tray.
TOM, twelve, the lamplighter's boy, sits cross-legged by the stove.
We are short eleven lamps on Gresham Row.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Twelve. I counted twice.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: Then twelve.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Sir, someone's cut them clean. Not smashed. Cut.
units.name: JOLLIFFE

units.text: Fuel was drawn on Thursday for sixty lamps. Fifty-eight were lit.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: Agatha, not now.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Mrs. Quill sets down the tray.
She pours tea for Agatha first, then Elias, then nobody.
Always the sums. Never the stairs.
units.name: MRS. QUILL

units.text: Mrs. Quill, what stairs?
units.name: TOM

units.text: Hush, boy.
units.name: MRS. QUILL

units.text: If this guild cannot keep the street lit, the parish will contract with the gas company.
units.name: JOLLIFFE

units.text: Gas. The smell of it.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: Then someone is paid to see the street dark.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: Constable, it was a rough night. You may go.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: I'd rather wait, sir.
units.name: JOLLIFFE

units.text: Elias stirs his tea.
Agatha turns a page.
Tom watches the stove.
The rain does not let up.
